products.name: Xiros Poly-Tape / Infinity-Lock, Jewel and Pitch-Patch soft tissue reinforcement devices
products.ownership_history: Xiros Ltd (UK); Xiros plc and Neoligaments Ltd both appear as earlier 510(k) applicants in openFDA. The sweep brief called this 'Xiros LARS'; Xiros and LARS are different companies (see lars-ligament).
products.composition: Permanent woven or warp-knitted polyethylene terephthalate (PET/polyester) tape, tube (Jewel) or patch (Pitch-Patch).

regulatory.reference: K222978 Poly-Tape/Infinity-Lock Soft Tissue Reinforcement Device (2022-12-27); K242237 Jewel (2025-07-15); K211563 Pitch-Patch (2021-08-13); K230671 Pitch-Patch (2023-05-31). Product codes QUW/FTL; Class II surgical mesh, 21 CFR 878.3300
on_label_indications: Poly-Tape/Infinity-Lock: reinforcement of soft tissues repaired by suture or other fixation during tendon and ligament repair including rotator cuff, patellar, Achilles, biceps, quadriceps, MCL, LCL, spring, deltoid, ulnar collateral ligaments or other tendons/extra-articular ligaments; not intended to replace normal body structure or provide full mechanical strength (K222978)
Pitch-Patch: permanent implantable device for reinforcement of rotator cuff tears (K211563)
Jewel: tubular mesh to support soft tissue repaired during ligament repair surgery, or to hold an allograft or autograft (K242237)

applications.evidence_summary: No published clinical study of Poly-Tape, Jewel or Pitch-Patch located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Permanent PET tape/patch is a different risk profile from resorbable scaffolds.
applications.caveats: Permanent synthetic; clearance rests on mechanical equivalence.

applications.evidence_summary: Pitch-Patch (K211563, K230671) is cleared for reinforcement of rotator cuff tears; no published clinical study located.
applications.caveats: No data.

bd.notes: Xiros's US presence is through 510(k) clearances; US distribution partner(s) not verified.

products.name: LARS synthetic ligament (Ligament Advanced Reinforcement System); LARS AC Band / ACJ
products.ownership_history: LARS device family; the 510(k) applicant was Corin USA for the LARS AC Band (K190143, 2019-11-04) and Movmedix S.A.S. for LARS ACJ (K253115, 2026-06-10). Corporate relationships among LARS SA, Corin and Movmedix not verified. The sweep brief said 'Xiros LARS'; Xiros (Poly-Tape) is a separate company.
products.composition: Permanent polyethylene terephthalate (polyester) fiber ligament with free intra-articular fibers and woven extra-articular segments (general description); the AC Band is a polyester tissue reinforcement band.

regulatory.reference: K190143 LARS AC Band Device (acromioclavicular fixation, 21 CFR 888.3030, product codes HTN/MBI); K253115 LARS ACJ (2026-06-10). No FDA clearance for LARS as an ACL/PCL graft was found in openFDA (2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: LARS ACJ / AC Band: indicated to provide fixation during the healing process following a syndesmotic trauma, such as fixation of acromioclavicular separations due to coracoclavicular ligament disruptions (K253115 comparison table)

products.challenge: US clearance covers acromioclavicular fixation only; ACL/PCL reconstruction with LARS is ex-US/off-label. The literature on LARS ACL is mostly from outside the US, with one 55-patient cohort showing a 33% mechanical failure rate at about 8 years.

applications.evidence_summary: LARS for primary ACL reconstruction: single-surgeon cohort of 55 at median 7.8 years had 33.3% mechanical failure (17/51) and 39% secondary procedures; authors say LARS should not be a primary ACL graft option (KSSTA 2019, Level III). Contrasting 2024 retrospective series (n=53, over 35 years) reported 3.8% failure, Lysholm 90.6, but 40% did not return to pre-injury activity. PCL meta-analysis (2022) considers it effective and comparable to hamstring autograft (limited evidence).
applications.caveats: Heterogeneous retrospective series; non-US mostly; US label is AC joint only, so these uses are not authorized.

evidence.title: Primary ACL reconstruction using the LARS device is associated with a high failure rate at minimum of 6-year follow-up
evidence.finding: Mechanical failure 33.3% (17/51) at median 7.8 years; 39.2% secondary operations.

evidence.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction with LARS Synthetic Ligament: Outcomes and Failures
evidence.finding: Lysholm 90.6, IKDC 80.3, failure 3.8% in patients over 35; about 40% did not return to pre-injury activity.

evidence.title: Ligament Advanced Reinforcement System (LARS) synthetic graft for PCL reconstruction: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: LARS for primary isolated PCL reconstruction seems effective and safe, comparable to 4-strand hamstring autograft; evidence limited.

bd.notes: US presence limited to AC joint clearances; K253115 (2026) shows ongoing US filings.

products.name: TenoGlide Tendon Protector Sheet (cleared as Tendon Wrap Tendon Protector)
products.ownership_history: Integra LifeSciences Corporation (Plainsboro, NJ). Integra announced TenoGlide 510(k) clearance and US launch in February 2007 (trade release); whether Integra still sells it was not verified.
products.composition: Absorbable porous matrix of cross-linked bovine type I collagen and glycosaminoglycan (GAG), a non-constricting protective sheet around injured tendons.

regulatory.reference: K053655 'Tendon Wrap Tendon Protector' (2006-02-03), product code FTM; mapping to the TenoGlide brand is inferred from the 2007 launch release and the identical composition - not stated in the summary read
on_label_indications: Indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue (K053655 summary)

applications.evidence_summary: 510(k) rested on physician experience, animal testing, biocompatibility and physical testing; the summary says clinical experience 'improves mobility of repaired tendons'. No published human comparative study of TenoGlide located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Label is protect/manage tendon injury; no randomized human data.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the procedure; low-cost sheet.
bd.notes: Cleared predicate for newer tendon protectors (Collagen Matrix wrap K080452 cites K053655 as predicate).

products.name: TenoMend Collagen Tendon Wrap
products.ownership_history: Collagen Matrix, Inc., now branded Regenity Biosciences. TenoMend is sold through Exactech (an Exactech page limits TenoMend sales to New Zealand); the FDA clearance is under the Collagen Matrix name. Regenity also sells private-label collagen tendon wraps. NeuroMend (nerve wrap; Stryker distribution since 2007) is a nerve product and is not recorded here.
products.composition: Resorbable type I collagen matrix sheet (non-constricting tendon encasement); when hydrated a conformable, porous collagen sheet.

regulatory.reference: K080452 Collagen Tendon Wrap (2008-05-15); predicates K053655 (Integra Tendon Wrap) and K060952 (Collagen Nerve Wrap)
on_label_indications: Collagen Tendon Wrap is indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue (K080452)

applications.evidence_summary: 510(k) was cleared on equivalence to Integra's Tendon Wrap; no clinical study of TenoMend located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Mapping between 'TenoMend' brand and K080452 comes from Exactech/search summary; US commercial availability not confirmed.

bd.notes: US availability uncertain; Exactech page lists New Zealand.

products.name: VersaWrap Tendon Protector / VersaCoat
products.ownership_history: Alafair Biosciences, Inc.; ownership not verified further.
products.composition: Bioresorbable clear hydrogel sheet of alginate and hyaluronic acid with a wetting solution, placed under, around or over injured tissue as a non-constricting interface (K240817).

regulatory.reference: K160364 VersaWrap Tendon Protector (2016-06-10); K200311 (2020-03-06); K240817 VersaWrap (2024-06-14); K251655 VersaCoat Tendon Protector (2025-07-18). Product codes OWW/FTM
on_label_indications: Indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue; may also be used in the management and protection of surrounding tissues such as skeletal muscle and ligaments (K240817)

applications.evidence_summary: Adu 2024 (Front Surg; Texas Tech hand surgery, retrospective, n=90 tendon repairs and tenolysis, mean follow-up 4.6 months): 92.3% good or excellent function (Strickland), active ROM 88.8%; no comparator. A University of Florida randomized zone 2 flexor tendon trial (NCT04322370, n=11) completed; a 400-patient Achilles trial (NCT07025252) is enrolling by invitation.
applications.caveats: Uncontrolled hand-surgery series; short follow-up; Alafair provided product to a preclinical comparison study (PMID 39306773, results not read).

evidence.title: Evaluating the effect of VersaWrap tendon protector on functional outcomes in operative tendon repairs
evidence.finding: 92.3% good or excellent function at mean 4.6 months; mean ROM 88.8% active.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Commercially Available Antiadhesion Tendon Protector Sheets in Tendon Repair Surgery Versus Tendon Repair Surgery Alone: A Preclinical Model Study
evidence.finding: Preclinical comparison of antiadhesion sheets (VersaWrap supplied by Alafair); results not read.

evidence.title: Prospective randomized blinded trial of VersaWrap Tendon Protector for zone 2 flexor tendon injuries (University of Florida)
evidence.finding: Completed; no results located.

bd.notes: Hydrogel antiadhesion sheet used in hand, Achilles, spine; K251655 VersaCoat adds a new brand.

products.name: Kerecis Tendon Protect (fish skin)
products.ownership_history: Kerecis Limited (Iceland). Coloplast acquired Kerecis in 2023 (general knowledge, not verified in this sweep).
products.composition: Solid sheets of North Atlantic cod fish skin (at least 0.4 mm thick) wrapped around the repaired tendon as a gliding barrier and scaffold for host tissue deposition.

regulatory.reference: K243843 (2025-06-04), product code OWY
on_label_indications: Kerecis Tendon Protect is indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue (K243843)

applications.evidence_summary: No published tendon-specific study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Kerecis's fish-skin graft has an RCT in diabetic foot ulcers (NEJM Evid 2024) that does not apply to tendon use.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is from wounds; the 510(k) rests on non-clinical testing.

bd.notes: New entrant (2025) in the tendon protector sheet segment.

products.name: Arthrex SpeedFLEX Implant (pre-sutured decellularized human dermis)
products.ownership_history: Arthrex, Inc. (Naples, FL); allograft donor processing referenced to LifeNet Health in the 510(k).
products.composition: Decellularized human allograft dermis pre-sutured with FiberWire passing suture and TigerLink SutureTape, four sizes, sterile single-use.

regulatory.reference: K251690 (2025-09-30), product codes OWY/GAT; primary predicate Medeor Matrix K103787 (porcine dermis), reference device MTF Fascia K120479 (allograft fascia, 510(k) 2012)
on_label_indications: Intended for general surgical procedures for reinforcement of soft tissue where weakness exists, and for reinforcement of soft tissues repaired by suture or suture anchors during tendon repair surgery including (but not limited to) rotator cuff, patellar, Achilles, biceps, quadriceps tendon (K251690)

products.challenge: First clear sign that a human dermal allograft patch took the 510(k) route (with a collagen xenograft predicate) rather than 361 HCT/P; it implies FDA may regard pre-sutured allograft dermis as a mesh device.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of SpeedFLEX located (cleared September 2025). Arthrex's ArthroFlex dermal matrix (see record) has one small nonrandomized comparative study.
applications.caveats: Newly cleared; no clinical data.

applications.evidence_summary: Label covers patellar, Achilles, biceps and quadriceps tendons; no clinical data.
applications.caveats: Newly cleared.

bd.notes: Positions Arthrex's catalog: ArthroFlex (361 allograft), SpeedFLEX (510(k) allograft), DX Matrix (xenograft).

products.name: Ortho-R (chitosan-based implant for rotator cuff repair)
products.ownership_history: Ortho Regenerative Technologies Inc. ('Ortho RTi'); the ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor is ChitogenX Inc. Entity relationship not verified.
products.composition: Lyophilized chitosan-based polymer solubilized with the patient's own PRP and applied at the rotator cuff repair site (company description; not verified).

regulatory.reference: US IND for a Phase I/II rotator cuff trial submitted 2021, FDA clinical hold August 2021 (CMC information), hold lifted December 2021. Registered randomized safety study NCT05333211 (n=78) status UNKNOWN
on_label_indications: None (investigational)

applications.evidence_summary: No published human study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23, 'Ortho-R'). Registered blinded randomized safety study NCT05333211 (n=78, started 2022-07, primary completion 2023-12, status unknown).
applications.caveats: Early stage; status unknown; sponsor claims unverified.

evidence.title: A blinded randomized controlled study investigating the safety of Ortho-R for rotator cuff repair compared with standard of care
evidence.finding: Registry status UNKNOWN; no results.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None located; registry last verified date old.

bd.notes: Small-cap biologic-polymer player; no 2026 update found.

products.name: NUsurface Meniscus Implant
products.ownership_history: Active Implants LLC (Memphis, TN per FDA panel minutes); CE-marked in Europe (2008) and used in Israel since 2011 (search summary). US trial sponsor on CT.gov: Phoenix Kinetics.
products.composition: Free-floating polycarbonate-urethane (Bionate) disc implanted in the medial compartment after a near-total medial meniscectomy; no fixation to bone or soft tissue.

regulatory.reference: US De Novo request (not PMA; the brief's 'PMA' is incorrect). FDA Orthopaedic and Rehabilitation Devices Panel, 2023-04-20, voted 2 yes / 6 no / 1 abstain on benefit outweighing risk. FDA Breakthrough designation (2019). A final De Novo decision was not located (no authorization found as of 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Proposed (De Novo): improve pain and function in the medial compartment of a knee in which the medial meniscus has been resected, in patients with mild to moderate arthritis, mild or greater knee pain, and cartilage present on the load-bearing surfaces (FDA panel minutes)

products.challenge: The sponsor's case rested on a post-hoc modified dataset (extrusion <5 mm and tibial spine height >=11 mm; 74 implanted vs 35 controls) after the full VENUS population; FDA reviewers noted a 34% automatic surgical failure rate falling to 17% in the subset and retrieval evidence of abrasion and fracture.

applications.evidence_summary: VENUS RCT (n=127 treated; NUsurface 61 vs non-surgical care 66): at 1 year KOOS Pain (P=.013) and KOOS Overall (P=.027) improved more with the implant. The sponsor's De Novo used pooled VENUS plus single-arm SUN (n=115): FDA panel voted against benefit-risk (2 yes, 6 no, 1 abstain) citing high failure rate, subgroup selection, and 2-year follow-up with sparse 60-month data.
applications.caveats: Randomized against non-surgical care (not against meniscus transplant or scaffolds); sponsor-funded; open-label; failure and removal rates high; 1-year paper above (2-year primary in the De Novo).

evidence.title: Treatment of post-meniscectomy knee symptoms with medial meniscus replacement results in greater pain reduction and functional improvement than non-surgical management: 1-year results of the VENUS RCT
evidence.finding: KOOS Pain and Overall improved more with NUsurface than non-surgical care at 1 year (P=.013, .027); treatment cessation 4.9% vs 14.5%.

evidence.title: Preliminary Results From a US Clinical Trial of a Novel Synthetic Polymer Meniscal Implant
evidence.finding: First 100 patients across VENUS and SUN at 12 months: greater KOOS gains than controls (119%-177% greater improvement), similar adverse event rates (16.9% vs 14.3%).

evidence.title: SUN: Safety utilizing NUsurface meniscus implant (single-arm)
evidence.finding: Completed June 2020; pooled with VENUS in the De Novo (Mercury dataset).

evidence.title: VENUS: Verifying the Effectiveness of the NUsurface System (randomized superiority study)
evidence.finding: Completed; registry n=34 differs from the 127 treated in the 1-year paper and the FDA minutes.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No FDA decision found; post-panel path unknown. NUsurface Implant Registry (NCT03953846) terminated 2023-11.

bd.notes: Fifth FDA attempt per trade coverage; a US launch looks unlikely without a new study.

products.name: Collagen Meniscus Implant (CMI; Menaflex; CMI XL)
products.ownership_history: ReGen Biologics Inc. 510(k) K082079 (ReGen Collagen Scaffold / Menaflex, 2008-12-18) was rescinded by FDA on 2010-10-14, pushing ReGen into bankruptcy; Ivy Sports Medicine (a ReGen investor) kept the product alive and later won on appeal 2-1 against FDA (dates not retrieved). Ivy obtained a new 510(k), K170364 (CMI XL, 2017-05-02). Stryker's Endoscopy division acquired Ivy Sports Medicine on 2016-09-01 (Ry Ortho). Whether Stryker actively markets CMI in the US today is not verified.
products.composition: Resorbable scaffold of type I collagen from bovine Achilles tendon, semilunar shaped, sutured to the meniscal rim.

regulatory.reference: K170364 Ivy Sports Medicine Collagen Meniscus Implant XL (2017-05-02), product code OLC; prior K082079 (2008-12-18) rescinded 2010
on_label_indications: Intended for use in surgical procedures for the reinforcement and repair of soft tissue injuries of the medial meniscus; the patient must have an intact meniscal rim and anterior and posterior horns for attachment of the mesh, and the surgically prepared site must extend at least into the red-white zone (K170364 and K242302 text)

products.challenge: The 2008 clearance was rescinded in 2010 (a rare FDA reversal); the 2017 clearance restored a US pathway. The pivotal RCT showed benefit in chronic but not acute patients, and the 20-year follow-up found no chondroprotection.

applications.evidence_summary: Rodkey 2008 (JBJS, RCT, 311 patients across two arms: acute n=157, chronic n=154; mean 59 months): implants produced new meniscus-like tissue and significantly increased meniscal tissue on second look (P=.001); clinical benefit (Lysholm, Tegner, activity) in the chronic group but none in the acute group. 20-year prospective case-control (n=36): no difference vs partial meniscectomy on Lysholm, KOOS, Tegner, IKDC or radiographic OA, so the implant was not chondroprotective. Meta-analysis of CMI vs Actifit (37 studies, 1,276 patients): both improve scores; failure risk 7% CMI vs 9% Actifit.
applications.caveats: ReGen-funded pivotal; most data are medial CMI in selected patients; modest effect, failure risk 7%; long-term chondroprotection not shown.

evidence.title: Comparison of the collagen meniscus implant with partial meniscectomy. A prospective randomized trial
evidence.finding: New meniscus-like tissue formed; chronic-group patients improved clinically with the implant, acute-group patients did not.

evidence.title: Loss of chondroprotection of medial collagen meniscus implant (CMI) at 20-year follow-up
evidence.finding: At about 21 years no clinical or radiographic advantage over partial medial meniscectomy; 1 failure per group.

evidence.title: No differences in clinical outcome between CMI and Actifit meniscal scaffolds: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Both scaffolds improved clinical scores; failure risk 7% (CMI) vs 9% (Actifit); evidence quality low.

evidence.title: Clinical outcomes and complications of a collagen meniscus implant: a systematic review
evidence.finding: 11 studies: Lysholm and VAS improved from 6 months to 10 years.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the arthroscopic procedure; coverage often limited by payer policies (not verified).
bd.notes: Stryker holds CMI after buying Ivy in 2016; low-volume niche.

products.name: RejuvaKnee Collagen Meniscus Implant
products.ownership_history: Collagen Matrix, Inc. is the 510(k) submitter; trade press attributes the announcement to Regenity Biosciences (rebranded company); Regenity said it would seek a strategic US commercialization partner (search summary).
products.composition: Semilunar implant of bovine type I collagen (nominally 99%) derived from meniscus, resorbable scaffold replaced by the patient's own tissue.

regulatory.reference: K242302 (2024-10-02), product code OLC (same as CMI)
on_label_indications: Intended for use in surgical procedures for the reinforcement and repair of soft tissue injuries of the medial meniscus; the patient must have an intact meniscal rim and anterior and posterior horns for attachment of the mesh (K242302)

applications.evidence_summary: No published human study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23); the company cites a 12-month animal study and cadaver work (press, unverified). Clearance relied on the CMI predicate.
applications.caveats: No clinical data; commercial partner unannounced.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed in the US yet (as of coverage).
bd.notes: Second US collagen meniscus implant after Stryker's CMI.

products.name: Actifit polyurethane meniscal scaffold
products.ownership_history: Orteq Sports Medicine; ownership/investors not verified. CE-marked and approved in Korea; FDA Breakthrough Device Designation reported; a US IDE has not been confirmed.
products.composition: Biodegradable, porous polyurethane scaffold fixed to the meniscal rim; designed for partial meniscus defects.

regulatory.reference: No FDA clearance/approval located; Breakthrough Device Designation reported (search summary); Orteq said it expected to present European clinical data to FDA
on_label_indications: Ex-US: partial meniscus defect scaffold (labeling not read). US: none.

applications.evidence_summary: Meta-analysis (37 studies, 1,276 patients incl. 804 Actifit): significant improvement and failure risk 9%; quality low, long-term Actifit data limited. French 5-year MRI/function study (n not recoverable) and a 54-patient multicenter series (VAS 5.5 to 2.9 at 24 months) are case-series level. Orteq reports >4,000 implants in 30 countries (company).
applications.caveats: Mostly case series; one independent RCT not found; Orteq-funded long-term follow-up planned (NCT07800923, n=120).

evidence.title: No differences in clinical outcome between CMI and Actifit meniscal scaffolds: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Both scaffolds improved symptoms and function; failure risk 7% CMI vs 9% Actifit.

evidence.title: Actifit polyurethane meniscal scaffold: MRI and functional outcomes after a minimum follow-up of 5 years
evidence.finding: 5-year MRI and function outcomes (abstract not indexed; findings not read).

evidence.title: Long-term follow-up of Actifit meniscal scaffold patients
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting; primary completion estimated 2028-09.

bd.notes: Ex-US hospital procurement; US entry blocked pending FDA data.
